## Press Release

### Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee, September 15-16, 2026

For release at 2:00 p.m. EDT 

The Federal Reserve on Wednesday released the minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting that was held on September 15–16, 2026.

The minutes for each regularly scheduled meeting of the Committee are generally published three weeks after the day of the policy decision. The descriptions of economic and financial conditions contained in these minutes are based solely on the information that was available to the Committee at the time of the meeting.

The minutes can be viewed on the Board's website.

“With regard to the outlook for monetary policy beyond the current meeting, most participants assessed that another increase in the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate by year end,” the minutes from the Sept. 15-16 meeting noted.

At that meeting, the FOMC voted unanimously to raise interest rates by a quarter point, to a range of 3.75 percent to 4 percent, in a bid to rein in persistent inflation. Annual inflation has been above the Fed’s 2 percent target rate for five-plus years.

# Fed minutes: Another rate hike likely coming this year to combat persistent inflation

 By The Associated Press October 7, 2026 | 2:18 PM 

WASHINGTON (AP) — Most Federal Reserve officials expect that another interest rate increase will likely be needed this year to combat inflation, according to minutes released Wednesday from the central bank’s most recent meeting. 

The officials unanimously agreed that inflation was still elevated and had not made much progress toward their 2% target in recent months, the minutes said. The Fed increased its key interest rate at the Sept. 15-16 meeting by a quarter-point to about 3.9%, its first increase in three years.

# Fed policymakers split over 25 bps hike rationale as most expect another increase in 2026

The September hike was unanimous, but officials differed on whether tighter policy was precautionary or needed to curb demand 

The Fed raised its target range to 3.75-4 percent as inflation remained above its 2 percent objective 

 Published: Thu 8 Oct 2026, 1:57 PM 

Federal Reserve policymakers unanimously agreed to raise interest rates in September but differed significantly over why tighter policy was needed, revealing an increasingly important debate over whether U.S. inflation is being driven mainly by temporary supply shocks or stronger underlying demand.

The Federal Open Market Committee raised its target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 3.75-4 percent at its September 15-16 meeting, with all 12 voting members supporting the decision.

# FOMC minutes: another hike still on the table

 Mira Chen · October 7, 2026 · 7 min read 

The Federal Open Market Committee’s September 15–16, 2026 minutes, posted on October 7, 2026 at 2:00 p.m. Eastern (18:00 UTC), do not read as a pause. All 12 voters had already raised the federal funds target range by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent. The new document adds the outlook: most participants judged that another increase would likely be appropriate by year end.

Bitcoin is not getting a hold signal from that text. It is getting a reminder that the September hike was a first step in a still-open path, not a finished cycle.

The minutes never mention Bitcoin, ether, or crypto. The rates path still sets the macro tape that Bitcoin’s recorded history has to live with.
